title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is handwritten on the back of a typescript sheet of SGA 7, Exposé IX (Grothendieck's monodromy pairing). The neighbouring 'pages' are that typescript and are mathematically unrelated to this note.

Setting, as far as it can be read: k is a base ring and s is a k-module, with a submodule s^+ and further data r_* (perhaps a filtration) and a parameter t. Grothendieck considers the functor k' -> s^{k'} = V(s)(k') = Hom_k(s,k') on k-algebras k', i.e. the 'vector bundle' V(s) attached to s. He defines, for each finite set I (or each n), a graded object A_*(s,s^+,r_*,t)(k')(I). This is an algebra of divided-power formal series in variables X_i (i in I) with coefficients in s^{k'}, tensored with the exterior algebra on the dX_i. It is taken modulo the ideal generated by sum X_i - t and sum dX_i. This is exactly the shape of the algebra of 'polynomial differential forms on the n-simplex' (Sullivan / Bousfield-Gugenheim), but with divided powers instead of polynomials. It is the 'divided power de Rham complex of the simplex', with the simplex equation sum X_i = t and the face/degeneracy structure in I.

Computation:
- Eliminating X_n and dX_n gives A_n(k') ≅ s^{k'}{{X_0..X_{n-1}}}[dX_0..dX_{n-1}].
- As a k'-module (not as an algebra) this is the product (s^{k'})^{N^n × P([0,n-1])}. The basis is divided monomials X^[α] times dX_J, with J a subset of [0,n-1].
- Functorially in k' this is Hom_k(s,k')^{N^n×P} ≅ Hom_k(s^{(N^n×P)}, k'), where the exponent in parentheses denotes a direct sum. That is V(s ⊗_k k[Y_0..Y_{n-1}] ⊗_k Λ(y_0..y_{n-1}))(k').

So each A_n is representable by the vector-bundle scheme of the module s⊗k[Y]⊗Λ(y). This uses the standard duality: completed divided powers are the dual of the symmetric algebra, and Λ is self-dual. The point is that the divided-power de Rham algebra of the simplex, viewed as a functor of k', is an affine (graded, alternating) scheme. Its coordinate module is the polynomial de Rham algebra on dual variables Y_i, y_i.

Next he studies the quotient A_n/A_n^+ ≅ s^{k'}/(s^{k'})^+, with a map from \bar s^{k'}, and the induced morphism A_n(k') -> V(\bar s)(k'). By Yoneda this corresponds to a module map \bar s -> s ⊗ k[Y] ⊗ Λ(y), compatible with the map coming from s.

Conclusion: A^n_*(s,s^+,r_*,t) = s ⊗_k k[Y_0..Y_{n-1}] ⊗_k Λ(y_0..y_{n-1}). It serves the 1976 IHÉS lecture's project of a divided-power (crystalline-flavoured) simplicial de Rham complex valid over arbitrary rings. It aims at computing cohomology of simplicial sets or homotopy types integrally or in characteristic p via 'forms on simplices', with the representing objects made explicit.
errors: The marginal notes are largely illegible, so the exact role of s^+, r_* and t is uncertain.

Notation slips between s^{k'}, Hom_k(s,k') and 'A^*_*' versus 'A_n' versus 'A^n_*'; the passage from product to direct sum (dualising) is stated without finiteness hypotheses. Hom_k(s,k')^{X} ≅ Hom_k(s^{(X)},k') is fine, but the identification of the functor with V(...) presumes the standard convention V(M)(k') = Hom_k(M,k').
The final formula identifies only the module/scheme structure. The multiplicative and differential structure (and the dependence on t) is not checked on this page.

ideas.what: Divided-power version of the simplicial algebra of polynomial differential forms on the standard simplices (Γ[X_0..X_n]⊗Λ(dX_i) modulo ΣX_i - t, ΣdX_i)
ideas.modern_name: divided-power (Γ-) polynomial de Rham forms on simplices; integral/characteristic-p analogue of Sullivan's ∇(•,•)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Sullivan (1977) for the rational version; integral/divided-power analogues to Cenkl–Porter (c. 1981) and later work on integral de Rham theorems
ideas.where_published: only the (unpublished) 1976 IHÉS lecture these notes belong to

ideas.what: Identifying the divided-power forms on the n-simplex, as a functor of k', with the vector-bundle scheme V(s⊗k[Y]⊗Λ(y)) via Γ/Sym duality
ideas.modern_name: representability / duality of divided power algebras with symmetric algebras (Γ = Sym^∨)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Roby, Cartan); duality Γ ↔ Sym standard
ideas.where_published: V(E) notation as in EGA I/II

missed.claim: Grothendieck, in 1975-76, was constructing a divided-power analogue of Sullivan-type simplicial de Rham forms over a general base. He treated it scheme-theoretically: each degree is an affine graded scheme V(s⊗k[Y]⊗Λ(y)). This anticipates integral/mod-p 'de Rham theorems for simplicial sets' via divided-power forms (Cenkl–Porter and later), a link not credited to him.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to the history of integral and p-adic models of homotopy types (divided-power or cosimplicial models, Mandell-type questions). It shows Grothendieck worked on a 'schematised' cochain algebra of simplices well before Pursuing Stacks.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a fragmentary but clear computation of divided-power de Rham forms on simplices made representable as affine schemes, from a little-known 1976 IHÉS lecture. The topic itself (divided-power polynomial forms) was later developed by others. The novelty is mainly historical, and the page is too fragmentary to show a finished new result.
transcription_corrections: The neighbouring 'pages' are the SGA 7 Exp. IX typescript on the reverse/underlying sheet and are unrelated to this note.

In the second display the completed divided-power symbol is applied with coefficients s^{k'}_*, roughly \widehat{Γ}_{s^{k'}}{{k'^I}} ⊗_{k'} Λ^*(k'^I/k'); the right-hand marginal note reads approximately 'idéal engendré par ΣX_i − t'.
Both annotations under the ≃ signs read 'comme foncteur en k''.
The note '(N^n × P([0,n−1]))' with superscript in parentheses denotes a direct sum (s^{(X)}), versus product (s^{k'})^{X} without parentheses.
Last line: 'On voit donc, que' / 'On voit donc, pour n' (uncertain).
